chunks: And by this chain of narrators, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh (peace be upon him),
he said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited that a funeral procession be followed by a censer.

key_terms.بِمِجْمَرَةٍ: with a censer (mijnmarah) — a vessel holding live coals over which incense or ʿūd is burned
key_terms.جَنَازَةٌ: funeral procession/bier — the body and its accompanying cortège carried to the place of burial
key_terms.نَهَى: he prohibited — a direct Prophetic nahy (prohibition), indicative of ḥurma (forbiddenness) in jurisprudential reasoning

ai.seo_question: What does a Shia hadith in al-Istibsar say about carrying a censer or incense burner during a funeral procession?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted via Imam al-Ṣādiq (AS) through a well-known Kufan chain, records a Prophetic prohibition against accompanying a funeral procession with a lit censer (mijnmarah — a vessel bearing burning coals used to produce incense smoke). Its placement in al-Istibṣār under the chapter on perfuming the funeral shroud (tajmīr al-kafan) contextualises the ruling: while fumigating the shroud itself before the procession may be permitted, carrying a censer in the procession is forbidden.
word_analysis: peace and blessings be upon him and his family
